questions.q: In `ga.addParam('sysparm_name', 'checkDateRange');`, what does `sysparm_name` specifically tell GlideAjax?
options: Which public method on the named Script Include to run
The name of the Client Script itself
The name of the field being validated
Nothing - it is an optional, cosmetic parameter
questions.explain: sysparm_name is the reserved parameter name GlideAjax uses to pick which method on the target Script Include executes.

options: It returns the server's answer directly as its own return value
It takes a callback function that runs later, once the server has responded - it is asynchronous
It blocks the browser until the server responds, then continues
It only works with XML-formatted ServiceNow tables
questions.explain: getXMLAnswer() is the real, standard asynchronous GlideAjax callback method - the answer is only available inside the callback, later.

options: g_form.addInfoMessage is not a real method
The `if` check runs immediately, before the server responds, so `result` is still undefined at that point
addParam was never called, so the request never sends
GlideAjax only supports boolean answers, not strings
questions.explain: Because getXMLAnswer is asynchronous, code after it (outside the callback) runs before the callback does - result is undefined when the if statement checks it.

questions.q: In `new GlideAjax('FreezeWindowChecker')`, what must `'FreezeWindowChecker'` match exactly?
options: The Script Include's `type` property
The name of the Client Script
The table the Client Script is attached to
The browser's current URL
questions.explain: The string passed to GlideAjax's constructor must match the target Script Include's type exactly, or the call cannot find it.

options: Because the check and the g_form call happen inside the callback itself, after the server has actually responded
Because it uses addParam instead of getXMLAnswer
Because g_form.addInfoMessage is synchronous and ignores timing entirely
There is no real difference between the two examples
questions.explain: Doing the checking and the form update inside the callback guarantees the server's real answer is already available by the time that code runs.
